questions.question: Which of the following classical dances begins with a drumming performance called "Kelikottu"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathakali**__.

__
 
• **Kathakali **begins with a **drumming performance** called **"Kelikottu"**.
 
• Kelikottu serves as a brief drumming passage heralding the commencement of the performance, typically held within **temple premises after nightfall**.
 
• Following Kelikottu is the **Todayam**, during which one or two characters seek the blessings of the gods.
 
• Subsequently, the Purappadu ensues, featuring a pure Nritya (dance) piece.
 
• During Kelikottu, the harmonious interplay of drums and cymbals accompanies the proceedings, enhancing the auditory experience.
 
• The drums employed in Kelikottu encompass a variety, including the resonant Kettledrum, the classic timpani, and the elongated Maddalam drum.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Odissi, **a classical Indian dance form, traces its origins to the sacred precincts of Odisha, an eastern coastal state of India.
 
• **Kuchipudi, **a captivating dance-drama, originated in the village of Kuchipudi, nestled in Andhra Pradesh, India.
 
• **Bharatanatyam, **another classical Indian dance form, has its origins in Tamil Nadu.

questions.question: To which of the following Gharanas did Hindustani Classical Vocalist, Bhimsen Joshi belong?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kirana Gharana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhimsen Joshi **belonged to the **Kirana Gharana**, a prominent **school of Hindustani classical music**.
 
• The **Kirana Gharana **is known for its emphasis on intricate **melodic patterns**, **slow and meditative style**, and use of the** 'gayaki ang' **or **singing style**.
 
• **Bhimsen Joshi's** music was shaped by the **teachings of his guru, Sawai Gandharva**, who was also **associated** with the** Kirana Gharana**.
 
• **Joshi's** rendition of **classical ragas** and **devotional compositions** showcased the aesthetic of the **Kirana Gharana**.
 
• His performances earned him **acclaim as one of the greatest vocalists in Indian classical music**.
 
• His legacy continues to **inspire aspiring musicians** and **enthusiasts** of **classical music worldwide**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agra Gharana**

 
 
• Emerged in the city of **Agra, Uttar Pradesh**, in **medieval Northern India**.
 
• **Established** by **Haji Sujan Khan**, a **court musician** of **Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan**.
 
• Has significantly impacted **Hindustani classical music**, **particularly vocal styles**.
 
• Includes **Faiyaz Khan**, **Vilayat Hussain Khan**, **Khadim Hussain Khan**, and **Sharafat Hussain Khan**.
 
 
 
• **Rampur Sahaswan Gharana**
 
 
• **Founded **in the princely state of **Rampur, Uttar Pradesh**, in the **19th century**.
 
• **Established** by **Ustad Inayat Hussain Khan** and **Ustad Mehboob Khan**, c**ourt musicians** of **Rampur**.
 
• Known for i**ntricate melodic patterns**, **rhythmic improvisations**, and **systematic presentation of ragas**.
 
• Includes **Ustad Mushtaq Hussain Khan**, **Ustad Nissar Hussain Khan**, and **Ustad Bade Ghulam Ali Khan**.
 
 
 
• **Gwalior Gharana**
 
 
• Emerged in **Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh, India**.
 
• **Established **by **musicians patronized** by the **Scindia dynasty rulers**.
 
• Includes **Ustad Haddu Khan**, **Ustad Nathu Khan**, **Ustad Hassu Khan**, and **Pandit Vinayak Rao Patwardhan**.
 
• Profound impact on **Hindustani classical music,** particularly **vocal styles and compositions**.

questions.question: Which of the following classical dances is known to be ekaharya, where one dancer takes on many roles in a single performance?

__
 
• **Bharatanatyam**, one of the oldest classical dance forms in India, is known for its unique feature of **Ekaharya**, where a single dancer portrays multiple characters in a single performance.
 
• The term **Ekaharya** derives from Sanskrit, meaning "one actor" or "one character," highlighting the versatility of the performer.
 
• This dance form uses intricate **abhinaya (expressive gestures)** and body movements to depict multiple roles, often supported by rich mythological narratives.
 
• Bharatanatyam, originating from Tamil Nadu, is deeply rooted in **Natya Shastra**, an ancient treatise on performing arts written by sage Bharata.
 
• It is a highly codified art form performed in temples as a form of devotion and later evolved into a stage performance art.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It is an ancient Indian treatise on performing arts attributed to sage Bharata, detailing various aspects of drama, dance, and music.
 
• It outlines the principles of Rasa (emotions), Abhinaya (expressions), and Mudras (gestures) used in Bharatanatyam.
 
 
 
• **Key Elements of Bharatanatyam:**
 
 
• **Nritta:** Pure dance movements without storytelling elements.
 
• **Nritya:** Expressive dance that conveys emotions and stories through gestures and facial expressions.
 
• **Natya:** Dramatic art, combining speech, music, and dance.
 
 
 
• **Ekaharya in Other Classical Dances:** While Bharatanatyam is prominent for Ekaharya, similar concepts can be seen in other forms like Kathak and Kuchipudi, though Bharatanatyam is most recognized for it.
 
• **Devadasi Tradition:** Historically, Bharatanatyam was performed by Devadasis (female temple dancers) as a form of devotion to deities in temples.
